The series shows a strong trend and moderate ranking; a softmax weight may regularize the inverse‑error extremes and still exploit the trend dominance.
Try a forward‐selection based weighted combination to see if a data‑driven subset improves over simple weighted or median, given moderate ranking stability and trend dominance.
The series is trend-dominated with moderate ranking stability; a simple mean may offer a different, unweighted combination that could outperform the weighted ones.
The series has moderate ranking stability and a strong trend; a weighted combination with a different weighting scheme may capture complementary strengths.
The series is trend-dominated with moderate ranking stability; a trimmed mean may reduce influence of a few high-error outliers and test a non-weighted alternative.
Use a metric‑ranked subset to reduce noise given moderate ranking stability; try a weighted combination on the best 7 models.
Test a weighted combination on the reduced pool4 using softmax_neg_error weights to see if a smoother weighting improves over inverse_error on the same pool.
The series is trend‑dominated with moderate ranking stability; a DBA (distribution‑aware) method might better capture the error distribution across models.
test a weighted combination on the full pool using the inverse_error handle (w6) to see if full diversity helps under strong trend dominance.
The series has a strong trend and moderate ranking stability; per‑horizon weighting may capture the slight horizon shift in best models.

decision.justification: Selected 'weighted on pool4 weighted by w5' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.327. Series context: trend strength 0.9283 and seasonal strength 0.2183; model ranking is moderate across windows (Kendall tau 0.329); 5 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 30.877.
